units.source_text: 柏木暗示的，或在我面前表演的人生，其生存和破灭只具有同样的意义。

en.t: The life that Kashiwagi hinted at, or performed before me, gave the same meaning to its survival and its destruction.

units.source_text: 在这种人生中，缺乏自然性，也缺乏像金阁那样的结构美。

en.t: In such a life, there was no naturalness, and no structural beauty like that of the Golden Pavilion.

units.source_text: 可以说，它只是一种痛苦的痉挛。

en.t: One might say it was nothing more than a painful convulsion.

units.source_text: 而且我完全被它深深吸引，在这里认准了自己的方向，这也是事实。

en.t: And it is also true that I was wholly and deeply drawn to it, and there recognized the direction I myself would take.

units.source_text: 不过，首先可怕的是，不得不用充满荆棘的生的碎片，让自己的手沾满鲜血。

en.t: Yet what was frightening first of all was that one had to stain one's own hands with fresh blood by using fragments of life filled with thorns.

units.source_text: 柏木以同样的程度轻蔑本能和理智。

en.t: Kashiwagi despised instinct and reason in equal measure.

units.source_text: 他的存在本身，犹如形状怪异的球，到处碰撞，企图冲破现实的墙。

en.t: His very existence was like a strangely shaped ball, colliding everywhere as it tried to break through the wall of reality.
This could hardly be called an act.

units.source_text: 总而言之，他所暗示的人生，是要打破那以求知的伪装蒙骗着我们的现实，为清扫出一个不再蕴含丝毫未知的世界而上演的一出危险的丑剧。

en.t: In short, the life he hinted at was a dangerous farce staged to smash the reality that deceives us under the disguise of seeking knowledge, and to clear out a world that no longer contained the slightest unknown.
